workflow_name: Expenses document date for later period v/s posting date in previous period / qtr
workflow_description: Flag line items where Document Date falls in a later accounting month-year than Posting Date, including across years, indicating potential timing irregularities.
business_logic_plan: Business Logic Plan: Expenses document date for later period v/s posting date in previous period / qtr Data Source FBL3N.csv Required Columns: ["Company Code", "Document Number", "Posting Key", "G/L Account", "Document Date", "Posting Date", "Amount in local currency", "Local Currency", "Document Type", "Text", "Document Header Text", "G/L Acct Long Text", "G/L Acct Long Text.1", "Cost Center", "Profit Center", "Reference", "Entry Date", "User Name", "Offsett.account type", "Offsetting acct no."] Business Requirements Q1: Which comparison should define the exception between Document Date and Posting Date? A1: Flag whenever Document Date month-year > Posting Date month-year (any later month, including across years) Q2: Should we exclude quarter-end accrual/provision entries from the exception list, or include all document types? A2: Exclude entries where G/L Acct Long Text contains 'PROVISION' (use G/L Acct Long Text) Q3: Do you want to apply a materiality threshold on Amount in local currency for exceptions? A3: No threshold – include all amounts (use Amount in local currency) Q4: Should we restrict the analysis to expense G/L accounts, or include all G/L accounts? A4: Include all G/L accounts (use G/L Account) Q5: Do you want to allow a month-end grace window so that near-cutoff postings are not flagged? A5: No grace window – flag all later month cases Q6: Do you want to exclude clearing/settlement-related postings from the exception list? A6: Exclude entries where G/L Acct Long Text contains 'Clearing' (e.g., 'GST Clearing A/c') Q7: Should the exceptions include both debit and credit postings, or only debits? A7: Include both debit and credit postings (use Posting Key) Q8: Do you want to exclude reversal entries from the exceptions? A8: Include all entries regardless of reversal indicators Q9: Does this output structure look good to you? A9: This output structure looks perfect - proceed with this Q10: Before I generate the complete business logic plan, is there anything else I should know? A10: No, I think we've covered everything - please generate the plan Business Logic Describe the BUSINESS RULES in plain language for finance/audit users: Rule 1: Flag line items where the Document Date falls in a later accounting month-year than the Posting Date. This includes cases crossing calendar years (e.g., Posting Date 2023-12 vs. Document Date 2024-01). Rule 2: Exclude entries that appear to be provisions/accruals by removing items where G/L Acct Long Text contains the term "PROVISION". Rule 3: Exclude clearing/settlement-related postings by removing items where G/L Acct Long Text contains the term "Clearing" (e.g., "GST Clearing A/c"). Rule 4: Include all G/L accounts. Do not restrict to expense-only accounts. Rule 5: Include both debit and credit postings. Posting Key is retained for context but does not filter the exceptions. Rule 6: No materiality threshold. Include all amounts regardless of size (absolute value). Rule 7: No month-end grace window. Near-cutoff postings are still reported if the Document Date’s month-year is later than the Posting Date’s month-year, even by one month and even if within the first days of the next month. Rule 8: Include reversal-related entries. Do not exclude based on reversal indicators in Document Header Text or reversal Document Types. Rule 9: For review clarity, derive and display: - Document Month-Year and Posting Month-Year - Month_Diff (number of months Document Date is later than Posting Date) - Document and Posting Quarters - A clear Exception_Reason note: "Document Date later than Posting Date (month-year)" Rule 10: The final exception population consists of items that meet Rule 1 and are not excluded by Rules 2 and 3. All other included rules govern scope and presentation. Output Columns Company Code: Legal entity identifier to understand which company the exception relates to. Document Number: Primary document ID to enable drill-down and traceability in the ledger. Posting Key: Indicates line-item nature and debit/credit; useful for understanding the entry’s direction and posting logic. G/L Account: Account impacted; essential to assess the nature of the cost/revenue and determine risk relevance. Document Date: The document’s original date; one side of the timing comparison. Posting Date: The accounting recognition date; the other side of the timing comparison. Amount in local currency: Monetary impact in company currency; needed to gauge materiality and prioritize review. Local Currency: Currency code to interpret the amount correctly. Document Type: Context on transaction type (e.g., vendor invoice, journal); aids in investigative follow-up. Text: Line-item narrative; helps understand the business purpose of the posting. Document Header Text: Header-level description providing additional context for the document. G/L Acct Long Text: Account description; shows why some entries might be excluded (e.g., "PROVISION" or "Clearing") and supports reviewer understanding. G/L Acct Long Text.1: Additional account classification/context to help categorize exceptions. Cost Center: Organizational owner of the expense; assists in routing queries and accountability. Profit Center: Performance reporting unit; useful for impact analysis and follow-up. Reference: Additional identifier to link with source documents or sub-ledger references. Entry Date: Operational entry date; supports timing analysis alongside Posting and Document Dates. User Name: User who posted the entry; important for control and responsibility assessment. Offsett.account type: Type of the offset account (e.g., vendor, customer, G/L); helps understand the counterpart of the entry. Offsetting acct no.: Identifier of the offset account; enables targeted follow-up with counterparties or sub-ledgers. Doc_MonthYear: Derived month-year from Document Date; clarifies the document’s intended accounting period. Post_MonthYear: Derived month-year from Posting Date; clarifies the recognized accounting period. Month_Diff: Calculated difference in months (Document minus Posting). Positive values indicate the Document Date is later; used to quantify timing gaps. Doc_Quarter: Quarter derived from Document Date; helps analyze quarter-end patterns. Post_Quarter: Quarter derived from Posting Date; supports quarter-based trend analysis. Exception_Reason: Standardized note stating why the item is flagged ("Document Date later than Posting Date (month-year)"); enables consistent reporting and filtering.
